bypass_paths.path: Direct request to the reconciliation API, bypassing the gateway
bypass_paths.evidence: The API's listener admits only the gateway's workload certificate and network policy admits only the gateway as a source. No fixture: a deployment control; the adapter-level bypass is MTLS-06 and COMMON-02.direct

bypass_paths.path: Connection to a terminated listener without passing through the terminator
bypass_paths.evidence: MTLS-23: the listener requires the terminator's certificate and refuses any other peer, with or without a valid agent certificate; cases MTLS-02 and MTLS-06

bypass_paths.path: Forwarded-identity headers: the forwarded-certificate header on a direct listener or from a peer that is not allowlisted, the ssl-client-* family, and any other header that names a client
bypass_paths.evidence: MTLS-24 and MTLS-26: only Cert of the forwarded-certificate header of an allowlisted terminator is read, and every other such header is ignored and removed; cases MTLS-01, MTLS-02, MTLS-03, MTLS-05, and MTLS-07

bypass_paths.path: Cleartext HTTP, or a TLS version below 1.3, on a claimed route
bypass_paths.evidence: MTLS-1: no such listener exists; case MTLS-08
MTLS-17: no tickets are issued or accepted and a resumed connection is refused; case MTLS-17

bypass_paths.path: A connection reused for many requests, or multiplexed, including after the status bound
bypass_paths.evidence: Every request passes the same enforcement points, with the identity re-read for the request (MTLS-18) and the connection status record (MTLS-19); cases MTLS-15 and MTLS-16

bypass_paths.path: Other listeners on the gateway host, such as health, metrics, or administration
The PACT endpoints of draft section 13.2 on the same listener that require native authentication, such as POST /pact/v0.1/requirements
bypass_paths.evidence: Served through the same listener and authenticate_native, so MTLS-1 to MTLS-31 apply to them; case MTLS-23

unsupported_forms: OAuth certificate-bound access tokens (RFC 8705 section 3) and OAuth mutual-TLS client authentication (RFC 8705 section 2): the certificate authenticates the workload and nothing more, and no token is read or checked against the certificate (MTLS-28)
SPIFFE and SPIRE: no SVID validation, no trust-domain bundles, and no Workload API; a certificate that carries a spiffe:// URI is treated as an opaque URI name of its pinned CA (MTLS-7)

Insecure peer-header forwarding, and every terminator form other than the Envoy forwarded-certificate header in text format: only MTLS-24 is accepted, and the ssl-client-* headers of nginx-based proxies are not specified in wire version 0.1 and are ignored (MTLS-26)
OCSP, fetched or stapled; delta, scoped, and indirect revocation lists; discovery of lists through certificate extensions: status is complete lists from configured locations (MTLS-10, MTLS-12)
TLS versions below 1.3, and every resumed session: MTLS-1 and MTLS-17

Telling agents apart when they share one certificate or workload identifier: one certificate-derived workload per agent, the default of identity-mapping section 5, and a workload with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error (MTLS-8)
Identity from subject text, from the common name, or from other name kinds (email address, IP address, other names, directory names), and wildcard names: MTLS-6 and MTLS-7
Re-authentication or status refresh inside an open connection: the status record of a connection is never refreshed (MTLS-19)

Any field of the I07 profile other than the workload identifier, such as the business-unit mapping, the runtime isolation attestation, and the purpose and operation relation: supplied by the deployment outside this profile, and only /attributes/environment/workload_id is claimed (MTLS-30)
Any route other than the one in protected_routes: not listed, so not claimed
Other listeners on the gateway host: excluded by their out_of_claim control in bypass_paths

membership_sources.source: Peer certificate status: the list snapshot of the issuing pinned CA, bound to the connection that presented the certificate
Enrollment registry (workload to agent and holder key binding)

residual_limits: Post-read: reconciliation data already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later revocation of a certificate or an enrollment, an executed operation is not undone by revoking its receipt, and no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed here with no bound

Revocation propagation, certificate: a revocation reaches a new connection, and every request on a terminated listener, within the publication interval plus the refresh lag of the reference configuration (360 s) after the decision to revoke; an open direct connection is ended within the status bound after the publication of the list that carries it (660 s after the decision) and serves requests on the status of an older list until then
Revocation propagation, enrollment: revocation, compromise mark, and rotation take effect at the next request, within the consistency domain of the registry
Revocation propagation, pinned CA set and terminator allowlist: withdrawal takes effect at the next request after the configuration is reloaded; the reload time is declared by the deployment

Name reuse: the identifier names a subject alternative name that a CA can issue to another subject after the workload is retired, and the enrollment then applies to the new holder of the name; a TLS-only impostor still fails the holder-key proof, and an administrator revokes the enrollment of a retired workload before its name is reissued

Terminated listener: the gateway verifies the certificate and its status from the forwarded Cert but cannot verify that the end client proved possession of its key to the terminator or see the age of that connection, and relies on the terminator obligations of MTLS-27; a terminator that passes on a header the client supplied defeats the identity

TLS key compromise: between the theft of a TLS key and the propagation of its revocation a thief can authenticate as the workload natively but cannot sign a PACT presentation, because the holder key is distinct

Revocation list transport: an attacker on the path can withhold lists or replay older ones; lists are signed by the pinned CA, withholding ends in DEFERRED once the snapshot is older than the status bound, and a replayed older list is not adopted over a newer one
Clock: a CA clock behind the adapter's clock only makes lists look older and fails closed, and one ahead by more than the 5 s skew makes the list unusable; no grace applies to expiry
